articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning and Vector-based Clustering Method to Achieve Energy Balanced in Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: Underwater acoustic sensor networks (UASNs) have a wide range of applications, such as water quality monitoring, ocean data collection and underwater resource exploration. In UASN applications, the management of energy is very important. Sensor nodes in UASNs are usually powered by batteries, which are very difficult to replace and replenish. Extending the life cycle by reducing the energy consumption of UASNs can reduce the network operation cost. Therefore, the energy management problem has become a popular research topic in UASNs. The efficiency of cluster routing in reducing the communication overhead between nodes in the network has been verified by dividing nodes into clusters and having the cluster header (CH) responsible for communicating with the base station and other nodes. However, if the cluster headers and paths are not properly chosen, the energy consumption of the nodes will be unbalanced, thus leading to premature death of the nodes. In this paper, a reinforcement learning and vector-based clustering (RVC) method is proposed to achieve energy balancing in UASNs. We use reinforcement learning and vector forwarding methods to select appropriate CHs and relay nodes to balance the node energy consumption based on the residual energy of the nodes, the transmission distance and the node density in the direction of the routing vector. The simulation results show that the method can effectively reduce the energy consumption of UASN nodes, achieve energy balancing, and extend the network survival cycle.

articleTitle: Fault Prediction Method for 5G Bearer Network Based on Graph Random Walk
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: With the development of 5G networks, the number and complexity of network devices have increased dramatically. Locating and predicting faulty network devices is an important way to ensure the normal operation of 5G networks. Existing methods usually require the use of large amounts of real-time data, which is unacceptable for widely distributed network devices. We propose a 5G bearer network fault prediction method based on graph random walk. By analyzing the association relationship of network devices’ alarm information, we construct an alarm association graph. Use the graph random walk method to learn alarm rules from historical alarm information and use it to predict faulty devices. We verified our method on real data from network service providers and achieved better results than existing methods.

articleTitle: Single Image Reflection Separation in Scenes with Light Source Only on One Side of the Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: The phenomenon of reflection superposition manifests itself as complex and prevalent in the real world, leading to the emergence of various simplified linear and non-linear formulas and related models. This study points out the limitations of existing models in scenarios where the light source is only on one side of the camera and conducts a theoretical, quantitative analysis of such scenarios. Based on this, we reconfigured the relevant parameters of the synthetic dataset used in training, compared them with the original settings, and contrasted them with the YTMT model. Experimental results show that the reconfigured parameters improve the model performance on our self-constructed dataset, especially in better understanding the high-level semantics of images.

articleTitle: Time domain convolutional network ocean surface temperature prediction model based on multi-feature fusion attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: Ocean surface temperature is a key factor in the interaction between the ocean and the atmosphere, and rising ocean temperature has the potential to change the global atmospheric circulation system, which in turn has profound effects on the global climate. Accurate prediction of sea surface temperature is of great significance to Marine ecosystems and global climate. Based on the time domain convolutional network, this paper first proposes an ATCN (Attention-based temporal convolutional networks) model of the time domain convolutional network based on the attention mechanism to study the one-dimensional time series. Then, a multi-feature fusion model AM-TCN (With attention-based multi-feature fusion temporal convolutional network) model is proposed to study multi-dimensional time series for the prediction of sea surface temperature in the Yellow Sea and Bohai Sea. In this paper, a total of 15997 sea surface temperature data of the Yellow Sea and the Bohai Sea from 30°N to 42°N and 117° E to 128 ° E for 43 years are obtained by using the reanalyzable values from the website of the European Centre for Medium Range Numerical Weather Prediction (ECMWF) from January 1979 to December 2021. Use the last 60 months (1,860 days) to predict the temperature for the next 12 months (372 days). In the study of one-dimensional time series, this paper compares the improved ATCN model with several mainstream deep learning models, and verifies that the deep learning model has the ability to predict a few anomalies. In the study of multi-dimensional time series, a multi-feature fusion model AM-TCN model is proposed, and the characteristics of El Nino-Southern Oscillation Index (Nino3.4 Index) and ANOM value are added for multi-variable collaborative prediction. The improved AM-TCN model not only occupies less memory, but also has the advantages of short running time. It also improves prediction accuracy. Four model evaluation indexes were adopted in the experiment, namely Mean Squared Error, Root Mean Squared Error and Mean Absolute Error. Coefficient of Determination-R-squared (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) was used to analyze the degree of fit between the predicted sea surface temperature and the real sea surface temperature. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the improved AM-TCN model can reach 98.54%. The prediction performance of the improved model increased by 1.03%, and the overall performance was stable and the accuracy was high.

articleTitle: Multi-modal Channel-attention for Vehicle RGB Image Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: Existing applications of vehicle detection and monitoring using RGB cameras suffer from low-light conditions where the quality of RGB vehicle images is low. In this paper we propose to reconstruct RGB vehicle images using pairs of RGB image and Infrared image captured by a dual RGB-Infrared camera, and present RIVIC, an RGB-Infrared imaged based Vehicle Image reConstruction scheme such that existing solutions on RGB images can still work even in low-light conditions.RIVIC exploits a multi-modal channel-attention mechanism on paired RGB and Infrared image. Specifically, two convolutional neural networks are firstly utilized on RGB images and Infrared images separately to generate 64-channel feature maps, respectively. These features maps are then concatenated and fed into a channel attention module. As a result, the fusion weights for different channels are computed while preserving the useful information from both visible and infrared images. These fused features subsequently undergo downsampling and upsampling processes, and eventually the reconstructed RGB image is generated. Extensive experiments in real-world scenarios show that the reconstructed RGB images have a high-quality as compared with the groundtruth RGB images, in terms of Structure Similarity Index Measure,Mutual Information,the first-order Entropy and the second-order Entropy.

articleTitle: Jamming Attack and Defense Based on Deep Learning in Cross-Technology Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: With the increase of IoT devices, wireless communication protocols occupy a large amount of spectrum. Due to limited spectrum resources, researchers have proposed using software defined radio management, which enables Cross-technology communication (CTC) of different protocols within the same frequency band (such as 2.4GHz) through changes in physical layer signals without a hardware gateway, greatly reducing deployment costs and computational overhead. However, research on CTC security is not comprehensive enough. In order to study the security issues of CTC, we implemented continuous jamming attack, reactive jamming attack and jamming attack based on deep learning in CTC systems, and further studied corresponding jamming attack detection and defense measures. We conducted extensive experiments using USRP, constructed CTC scenarios, and introduced Channel State Infomation (CSI) as signal features for channel prediction, By using deep reinforcement learning algorithms to train CSI data and predict channel states, we can effectively defend against jamming attack signals and improve the performance of CTC.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Maximization in IRS-Assisted Wireless Powered MEC Systems With NOMA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: The integration of mobile edge computing (MEC) and wireless power transfer (WPT) effectively provides a robust solution to overcome the limitations imposed by the computational capacity and battery lifespan constraints of wireless devices (WDs). Nevertheless, the effectiveness of WPT and computation offloading cannot be guaranteed if the channels between the hybrid access point (HAP) and the WDs are obstructed. Therefore, intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is implemented to boost system performance, complemented by the adoption of non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) protocol to further enhance spectral efficiency. We investigate the maximization of energy efficiency of NOMA-based IRS-assisted WP-MEC systems while ensuring task queue stability in this article, which optimizes the reflection co-efficient matrix of IRSs during WPT and computation offloading stages, along with adjusting the CPU frequency and transmission power of WDs. A novel Lyapunov-based heterogeneous agent proximal policy optimization (LyHAPPO) algorithm is proposed to guarantee stability and exploit heterogeneous agent reinforcement learning, allowing the presence of different kinds of agents in the system to make appropriate decisions. The effectiveness of our proposed algorithm is evidenced by experimental results.

articleTitle: MaskCore: Towards Precise Semantic Segmentation in Industrial Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: In modern manufacturing, a significant challenge in applying deep learning to industry surface defect detection is the scarcity of defect samples and the diversity of abnormal types. This paper introduces MaskCore, a semi-supervised anomaly detection algorithm for industry surface defect detection. MaskCore addresses the current challenges of image feature lacking industrial semantic bias, under-represented local features, and coarse anomaly segmentation. First, self-supervised learning extracts features with industrial image semantic bias through feature adaptor. Second, semantic patch extraction enhances representation at object level. Lastly, the anomaly score is generated based on pixel-level anomaly segmentation via SAM (Segment anything model). We curated an industrial lens dataset, PhoneLens, with smaller surface anomalies surpasses that of available benchmark datasets. Our results show state-of-the-art performance on MVTec AD benchmark dataset, with 97.6% classification AUROC and 97.4% segmentation AUROC. On PhoneLens dataset, MaskCore outperforms the benchmark with 88.3% classification AUROC and 94.7% segmentation AUROC, highlighting its efficacy in industrial anomaly detection.

articleTitle: LCPTCN: Lightweight Temporal Convolutional Network with Cross-Group Pruning for Dynamic Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: The swift development of cloud platform services has led to the emergence of diverse workloads. Accurately predicting these varied and dynamic workloads while minimizing the computational resource demands of the forecasting model is crucial for efficient deployment and resource allocation on cloud platforms. To tackle the issues of complexity and high computational demands presented by traditional load forecasting methods, we propose a Lightweight Temporal Convolutional Network with Cross-Group Pruning for dynamic load forecasting (LCPTCN). We develop a Cross-Group Pruning Strategy (CGPS) to minimize redundant connections among the dilated causal convolutions within the Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN). Subsequently, LCPTCN integrates a gating mechanism to manage the proportion of temporal feature information flow and introduces the Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) mechanism to reduce the loss of feature information. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that LCPTCN surpasses comparative models in forecasting performance, computational efficiency, and parameter count.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Multi-UAV Topology Control, Offloading and Path Planning in Air-Space Edge Computing Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: In the event of an emergency, such as a post-disaster response scenario, uploading information to the edge cloud for processing can often result in considerable delays. In such contexts, the utilization of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted edge computing emerges as a viable solution to minimize the time taken for information processing. In this paper, we aim to establish a comprehensive data acquisition system, encompassing UAV swarms, ground users, and satellites. Specifically, during emergencies, satellites will be instrumental in planning the trajectory of the UAV swarms based on the observed disaster scene, including signal points to be collected and potential obstacles. This approach has the potential to significantly reduce rescue time and mitigate losses. Given the intricate nature of the proposed problem, which is influenced by numerous factors, a straightforward convex optimization approach is insufficient. Instead, we adopt a distributed approach to tackle the problem in two distinct parts. Firstly, we establish a fixed topology for the drones, and resolve the associated challenges through the application of a suitable control protocol. Secondly, we focus on optimizing the overall system’s energy loss. This is achieved by reformulating the problem as a Markov decision-making process (MDP) and subsequently addressing it through the application of a deep-Q-network (DQN).

articleTitle: Acoustic Imaging of Underwater Moving Targets Based on Inverse Synthetic Aperture Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: The morphological imaging and motion estimation of underwater dynamic targets are highly valuable in numerous application scenarios. However, many applications face challenges in deploying and maintaining expensive equipment, making it difficult to implement existing array and sonar-based solutions. In this paper, we propose a low-cost underwater dynamic target imaging system based on a pair of transducers(single-input single-output, SISO). We first extract target echo through Moving Target Indication(MTI) filter. The compensation for the radial distance of moving targets is executed by estimating their motion state. A joint time-frequency analysis(JTFA) method is used for instantaneous Range-Doppler(R-D) imaging. Additionally, a data augmentation method is designed to enable precise classification and identification of underwater moving targets with fewer samples. We conducted extensive simulations and practical experiments in an anechoic pool, successfully achieving acoustic imaging of moving targets with various shapes underwater. The average recognition accuracy for underwater dynamic objects with various shapes is achieved 94.28% in simulation and 79.92% in field experiment respectively.

articleTitle: Secure Skyline Group Queries Based on Encrypted Dominance Graphs in Cloud Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: In this paper, we define and investigate the secure skyline group query problem and propose a method named Secure Skyline Group Query processing based on Dominance Graph (DGSSGQ), which aims to efficiently find the skyline groups on encrypted datasets. In DGSSGQ method, we first present the data preprocessing and encryption mechanism based on dominance graphs, which record the dominance relationships between points in the dataset. To save the query processing costs, we further present the maintenance of the encrypted dominance graph. To achieve secure calculation on the encrypted DG, we design Secure Inclusion Protocol (SIP), which enables the determination of the inclusion of the nodes in the DG in a group. Based on the encrypted DG and SIP presented, we propose the secure skyline group query processing method to find the skyline groups. Thorough analysis shows the security and complexity of the proposed query methods, and the results of extensive experiments on real and synthetic datasets illustrate the performance of our proposed methods.

articleTitle: Forecasting Sudan Gold Prices with a Hybrid Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: As a crucial element of the financial market, the price creation process of gold futures has attracted the attention of academicians and financiers alike. However, given the time series data’s disorganized, chaotic, and non-stationary nature, predicting the price of gold futures is extremely difficult. This paper introduces a novel approach for forecasting gold prices by combining a Time-Series Mixer (TSMixer), Long Short Term Memory Neural Networks (LSTM), and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). Our proposed method addresses the challenges posed by characteristics of gold price time series data. Our model consists of three key components: a Mixer block for extracting temporal patterns, an LSTM component to leverage the sequential order of daily gold prices, and a CNN component to capture local patterns and abstract spatial features. By integrating these elements, our model offers a thorough method to tackle the difficulties involved in gold price forecasting, taking into account the data’s temporal and spatial patterns. Our study focused on Sudan Gold futures as our task and selected gold futures data from the Sudan Gold Refinery company from January 6, 2015, to December 22, 2022. Through comparative analysis with baseline methods, our experiments show that our model outperforms all other baseline models. These findings highlight the superior performance of our model in effectively predicting Sudan Gold futures.

articleTitle: Computing on Surface: A Multi-Task Multi-Access Offloading Scheme in Maritime Edge Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: The recent development of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) technology has been envisioned as a promising paradigm to cater for the growing maritime activities. However, the increasing growth of marine services poses challenges for processing maritime data. In this paper, we propose a surface computing paradigm in maritime networks, in which multi-task sensed by UAVs can be offloaded to multiple beacon stations. Multiple UAVs can process their workloads locally or offload to surface computing. Taking the system welfare and energy consumption into consideration, we present an optimization problem to determine the selection of beacon stations and the offloading decision, with the objective of maximizing the system welfare. We propose a hybrid auction and convex optimization approach to address the formulated problem. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed algorithms compared to several baselines.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Based Energy Consumption Minimization With Virtualization in Maritime UAVs-Assisted MEC Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: The flexibility and efficiency of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have been recognized as a viable solution to address the deficiency of deployment on the maritime mobile edge computing (MEC) networks. However, the limited computing resources of edge servers cannot support parallel processing tasks without performance loss. In this paper, we use virtual machine (VM) multiplexing technology to consider the performance degradation of parallel processing tasks in the UAVs-assisted MEC network. To ensure efficient task offloading, we focus on the trajectory planning and resource management for UAVs. Our objective is to minimize overall energy consumption while ensuring that time delays for all tasks are within tolerable limits. We first transform the joint optimization problem into a Markov Decision Process (MDP), then propose a Multi-Agent deep reinforcement learning-based Resource Management and Trajectory Planning (MA-RMTP) algorithm to solve the problem. The simulation results show that our proposed approach can significantly reduce the overall energy consumption compared to other benchmarks.

articleTitle: Who is Under the Spotlight in Peer Review Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: The practice of peer review has a long-standing history, remaining central to the academic assessment of personnel, projects, and awards to this day. Despite the universal application of peer review across different evaluative contexts, the processes for deriving outcomes vary, leading to instances where the targeted feedback from a minority of peers disproportionately influences the final decision, essentially serving as a significant lever for specific evaluations. Recognizing this, our work analyses and explores scenarios in project evaluations where a few dissenting peer opinions diverge markedly from the majority. To deal with this problem, we propose a novel method, namely Ranked Cosine Similarity for Peer Review (RCS-PR), which leverages cosine similarity measures to analyze agreement levels among peer reviews and identify divergent opinions effectively. By finding outlier peer review contributions and isolating certain projects, the method demonstrates notable effectiveness and practicality when applied to actual data, streamlining the peer review process while mitigating undue minority influence.

articleTitle: Edge-Assisted Low-Latency Object Detection for Networked Vehicles Using Point Cloud
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: In this paper, with the objective of enhancing the perception quality for autonomous vehicles based on point cloud data, we design an edge-assisted on-road perception framework. This framework contains three modules: adaptive point cloud transmission, driving environment complexity evaluation, and perception task scheduling. In specific, to suppress the transmission delay posed by fluctuating wireless links, we finely configure the quality of point cloud data to be transmitted with sampling and compression fidelity tuning. Then, taking the driving environment complexity into consideration, we propose perception score, a novel perception quality evaluation metric, according to which the edge server schedules the received tasks. Furthermore, an overall perception score maximization problem is formulated to obtain the optimal scheduling strategy at the edge. At last, a greedy-based time window constraint algorithm is designed, which can solve the problem at low computational complexity. Extensive experiments show that, compared to other benchmarks, our algorithm exhibits significant advantages in precise and low-latency object detection for autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Cooperative Action Decision based on State Perception Similarity for Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: In practical applications, implementing reinforcement learning in multi-agent environments is very important. Most of the existing multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms lack communication capabilities, forcing agents to learn solely from their local observations. Some reinforcement learning algorithms that include communication also limit the number of communicating individuals. We propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm that incorporates a local communication mechanism. This algorithm does not need to limit the number of individuals with whom the agent communicates. The agent can communicate with any number of agents in each time step, and the agent can choose whether to communicate and with whom to communicate. Besides, this algorithm requires no additional communication content and only uses the information obtained by the agent from the environment. Compared with recent methods, this method makes better use of the environmental information that the agent can obtain and plays a greater role in the team. This makes the actions of multi-agents more in line with human group actions. To verify the effect of our algorithm, we conducted experiments on several mature open-source multi-agent reinforcement learning environments. The experimental results show that our algorithm is better than MADDPG and M3DDPG.

articleTitle: Maximizing Profits with ON/OFF Multi-Server Configurations in Distributed Edge Clouds
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT), smart devices have generated large volumes of data and requests, surpassing the capabilities of traditional cloud computing paradigms to meet user requirements. Edge computing, enabled by distributed edge clouds (ECs) in urban areas, offers low-latency and bandwidth-efficient services for IoT devices or end-users. By implementing a multi-server configuration scheme that transitions servers between sleep mode and active state through ON/OFF operations, energy consumption costs can be significantly reduced while maintaining the profit based on service level agreements (SLAs). In this way, we develop a mathematical model for optimizing the multi-server ON/OFF schedule problem within the context of distributed ECs to maximize profits for the edge service provider (ESP). To address this problem with the exponentially high computational complexity and coupling characteristics, we propose a QMIX-based method for configuring multiple servers. Our method is capable of adapting to time-varying and fluctuating user request loads in different areas while making real-time decisions regarding multi-server ON/OFF operations. Experimental results obtained under realistic environmental conditions using real-world user request loads demonstrate that our approach can significantly increase the ESP’s profit.

articleTitle: An Improved BBR Algorithm with Adaptive Congestion Control for LEO Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks are favored for their global coverage, low latency, and geographical flexibility, but they also face challenges of high dynamism in network topology and congestion control. To address these issues, this study introduces an improved BBR congestion control algorithm (Deep-BBR) based on traffic prediction. The algorithm integrates Long Short-Term Memory networks, Graph Convolutional Networks, and attention mechanisms to accurately predict bandwidth utilization and dynamically adjust pacing gains. Experimental results show that the Deep-BBR algorithm significantly outperforms the traditional BBR algorithm in effective throughput, latency, and in-flight data management, effectively enhancing the communication performance and stability of LEO satellite networks. This improvement offers a more efficient and intelligent solution for congestion control in LEO satellite networks.

articleTitle: Two-Timescale Optimization for Task Offloading based on Sharded Blockchain in Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cloud and Network Computing (ICCNC)
abstract: Device-to-Device (D2D) task offloading is a key technique in edge computing, enabling nearby idle user devices to assist with computational tasks, thereby enhancing overall system efficiency. However, the reliability of idle devices is often overlooked in existing research. Blockchain, characterized by its tamper-resistant property and distributed architecture, is widely integrated into edge computing systems to ensure a trustworthy and reliable edge environment. Nevertheless, the substantial transaction volumes in D2D offloading scenarios present significant challenges to blockchain efficiency. In this paper, we propose a solution that leverages blockchain to evaluate the reliability of idle devices. Additionally, we introduce a blockchain sharding strategy to enhance transaction processing efficiency. Moreover, we consider the differences in decision-making frequencies between edge computing and blockchain by introducing a novel two-timescale model. This model enables timely task processing decisions at a fast timescale while accomplishing blockchain consensus at a slower timescale. Furthermore, we formulate an optimization problem that aims at maximizing the utility of user devices and ensuring efficient blockchain operation. Finally, we introduce a Two-Timescale Mixed Action Spaces Deep Reinforcement Learning (2Ts-MATDRL) algorithm to solve the problem across two timescales. Through simulation experiments, we validate the effectiveness of our proposed scheme.
